title: Stuff Smith in Chicago and Hollywood; Kirkeby gets him out of Fats's band
summary: After Fats he played with Stuff Smith in Chicago and at the Trouville Club in Hollywood with Buddy Rich, while Kirkeby had kept him out of the Waller band; he saw no sign Fats was ill.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah, it's been quite a while there. Because before that, before -- after I left, I went with Stuffy Smith and played Chicago, and after Chicago I went with Stuff Smith to Hollywood, and played the Treuville Club, and at that time Fats was moving. John Hamilton, Bugs was with Fats. They played the hotel in Chicago -- (Snap).
Congress Hotel?
Huh?
Congress?
No. No. No. They were recording -- I mean they were broadcasting, I can't -- and --
Sherman.
Sherman.
Sherman, that's the one.
Yeah.
Panther Room. Anthony.

Yeah, that's right. And I followed -- I was with Stuffy, and I went on -- I was with Stuff and the Kirkaby -- that was Kirkaby's doings. Yeah, Kirkaby was glad to get me out of the band. So he had to keep me out of there.
Oh, that was Kirkaby getting you out.
I see.

Yeah, you see, so -- and Johnny Buggs was there. They going to have -- he was scared to look me in the face, because of a lot of reasons, because I knew him backwards, and anyway, well, we won't go into that.

And so I went out to Hollywood, in the Trouville Club. Bergs Trouville Club, with Stuff Smith, and Buddy Rich, and all of us, did a jam session out there on, you know, how the heck was -- I've got a picture of Buddy Rich, and all that sort of thing. And Stuff Smith playing, and his violin, and oh, it was really nice. You know.
Then, came back and -- no, it was after Chicago. I came back and then I got my own group, and I went to Philadelphia and Fats was out there doing this picture, and then he passed.
Did you -- the last times that you saw Fats, did you have any idea that he was this sick? That it could happen to him?
No. No.
He didn't seem any different to you at all?
No, no, no. No, he wasn't ailing, no. It was just one of those things.
Just one of those things that happen.
Uh-huh.
